lines.trans: Oh, so you are the one directing that pilot!
Ah yes, though they have not told me the timeslot yet—Senior Tae-ho promised to clear out whichever weak slot he found.
That weak slot is us?! It is our slot you guys are moving into!

words.gloss: I am telling you it is us

lines.trans: Oh, right… casting guests was really tough.
Tell me about it—casting is brutal.
So we only barely managed to book Suzy and Taeyang from BigBang…
You call that struggling with casting?! Did the shoot turn out well?
We barely had time to prepare—yet surprisingly, the footage is super funny!
Maybe because nothing was scripted, tons of spontaneous moments popped up—if we structure the edit well, it looks promising!

lines.trans: Oh, right… casting guests was really tough.
Tell me about it—casting is brutal.
So we only barely managed to book Suzy and Taeyang from BigBang…
You call that struggling with casting?! Did the shoot turn out well?
We barely had time to prepare—yet surprisingly, the footage is super funny!
Maybe because nothing was scripted, tons of spontaneous moments popped up—if we structure the edit well, it looks promising!
See you next time!

meanings.note: Used in -(으)ㄴ/는 것 같다 to express 'it seems that...' or 'I think...'.

meanings.en: to be the same, to be like
meanings.note: Compares two things with -와/과 같다.

examples.trans: I think I'm late.
It looks like it's going to rain.

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

meanings.note: Used as adverb (겨우).

examples.text: 내 인생은 이제 내려갈 일밖에 안 남았어요. 겨우 스물셋인데 나 그동안 올라오기만 했어요.
examples.trans: Nothing remains in my life now except going downhill—I am barely twenty-three, yet all I have ever done is climb up.
I thought it over again (barely, only).

meanings.note: Indicates that something will happen in a very short time.

examples.trans: The bus will arrive soon.
I will contact you again soon.

괜찮다.gloss: to be fine; to be okay

meanings.en: to be fine; to be okay; to be alright
meanings.note: Used to reassure someone, decline an offer politely, or say something is acceptable.

examples.trans: I'm really fine.
Is it okay if we meet tomorrow?
Did you hear about this lineup, composition?
I was busy today because of lineup, composition.

meanings.note: adverb therefore

examples.trans: So how is it?
So I went.

그러다.gloss: to say so; to do so

meanings.en: to say so; to speak like that
meanings.note: contracted from 그러하다; often follows quoted speech

meanings.en: to do so; to act like that

examples.trans: Who said that?
That friend also said they are going together.

그렇다.gloss: to be so, to do so

meanings.en: to be like that, to be so
meanings.note: ㅎ-irregular; also used as a pro-verb ('do so / say so')

examples.trans: Is that really so?
Don't keep acting like that.

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그런데; introduces a contrast or obstacle.
Used to shift the topic in conversation.

examples.trans: By the way, what time is it now?
I want to go. But I don't have time.
Do you have time today?
Where are you going?

meanings.note: Used only with close friends, younger people, or children

examples.trans: Did you hear about this you guys?
I was busy today because of you guys.

meanings.en: video recording, television taping or shoot
meanings.note: Often paired with 하다 (녹화하다, 'to record/tape').

examples.trans: There is a shoot this afternoon.
The taping finished late.

meanings.note: Used for time or order.

examples.trans: Let's meet next time.
The next station is Seoul Station.

meanings.note: Bound noun referring to a location.

examples.trans: I have no place to go.
I have no place to go. (2)

meanings.note: Used as noun (돌발).

examples.text: 짜고 하지 않아서 그랬는지 돌발 상황도 되게 많고 구성만 잘하면 괜찮을 것 같아요!
examples.trans: Maybe because nothing was scripted, tons of spontaneous moments popped up—if we structure the edit well, it looks promising!
This point about unexpected, spontaneous is really important.

meanings.note: Common colloquial intensifier in spoken Korean

examples.trans: The weather is really cold today.
That food is really delicious.
I want to went inside right now.
How about trying to went inside together tomorrow?
I want to fall off, you know right now.
How about trying to fall off, you know together tomorrow?

meanings.note: Used as volitional quotative (뚫어주겠다고).

examples.text: 아 예, 시간을 얘기 안 해주네. 태호 형이 어디 약한 데 있으면 뚫어주겠다고 했는데.
examples.trans: Ah yes, though they have not told me the timeslot yet—Senior Tae-ho promised to clear out whichever weak slot he found.
Let us do that (would pry open for us) right away.

meanings.en: to be many, numerous, or abundant
meanings.note: Used for both countable and uncountable nouns.

examples.trans: Because it's the weekend, there are many people at the department store.

examples.text: 오늘 해야 할 일이 너무 많다.
examples.trans: There is too much work to do today.

meanings.note: Placed before a verb to express inability or impossibility.

examples.text: 어제는 너무 피곤해서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.trans: I was so tired yesterday that I couldn't sleep.
Because it rained, we couldn't go on the picnic.

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch
meanings.note: Primary meaning.
Idiomatic in 시험을 보다.

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.

meanings.note: noun situation

examples.trans: Situation is good.
Situation is bad.
Did you hear about this is casting?
I was busy today because of is casting.

meanings.note: Available time or duration.
Used with native Korean numbers to count hours (한 시간 = one hour).

examples.trans: Do you have time?
It takes two hours.

meanings.note: Expresses sudden realization, surprise, or hesitation.

examples.trans: Ah, yes.
Oh, I see!

meanings.note: Short-form negation placed directly before verbs and adjectives

examples.trans: I'm not going to the office today.
I haven't watched that movie yet.

않다.gloss: to not do, to not be

meanings.en: to not do, to not be
meanings.note: Auxiliary negative verb/adjective used after -지 (long-form negation)

examples.trans: The weather isn't cold today.
I didn't say anything.
The atmosphere today is really is weak.
That person always looks is weak.

meanings.note: dummy

examples.trans: dummy trans 1
dummy trans 2

meanings.note: Interrogative pronoun for location.

examples.trans: Where is the restroom?
Where are you right now?
This problem is too difficult.
Yes, that's right.

없다.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.en: to not exist, to not be present

examples.trans: I don't have time right now.
The tickets are all sold out, so there aren't any.

meanings.note: Slightly more formal/deferential variant of 네, commonly used when speaking to a boss or superior.

examples.trans: Yes, understood.
Yes, I will prepare it right away.

meanings.note: 1st person plural pronoun; also used for 'my' with family, school, or workplace

examples.trans: Our team has a good atmosphere.
Let's eat lunch together tomorrow.
I want to funny and right now.
How about trying to funny and together tomorrow?

meanings.note: Used as noun + causal copula (의외라서.).

examples.text: 아니 그런 얘기가 아니고요, 의외라서. 피디님, 저 물 좀…
examples.trans: No, I did not mean that—it was just unexpected. Producer, could I have some water…
This point about because it was unexpected is really important.

있다.gloss: to exist, to have, to stay

meanings.en: to exist, to be (in a place)
meanings.note: Opposite of 없다.
Marks the possessed item with 이/가.

examples.trans: Do you have time?
Nobody is at home.

related.gloss: to not exist, to not have

examples.trans: Listen closely to what I explain.
I eat Korean food well.

meanings.note: verb do well

examples.trans: Study well.
You did well.

examples.text: 웃겨? 야, 넌 남자 아니냐? 내일 촬영 준비나 해.
examples.trans: Funny, aren't you a man too? Go get ready for tomorrow's shoot.
The topic of preparation came up during this shoot.

짜다.gloss: to put together, to organize, to plan

meanings.en: to put together, to organize, to draw up
meanings.note: used for assembling a team, schedule, or plan
literal meaning of pressing liquid out

examples.trans: I planned the travel schedule in advance.
We need to reorganize the team.

meanings.note: Used as loanword + subject (파일럿이).

examples.text: 그럼 대체 편성? 그게 그 얘기지! 우리 거 죽이고 파일럿이 됐다 그 얘기 아니야 지금!
examples.trans: Replacement scheduling, then? That is the exact same thing—killing our episode so a pilot airs instead!

examples.text: 파일럿이 이번 달까지 방송이 돼야 된대요. 이게 또 협찬처 문제도 걸려 있고 그런가 봐.
examples.trans: They say the pilot must air before the month ends—apparently sponsor obligations are tied up in it too.

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.

meanings.note: Compound of 하다 (to do) and 주다 (to give).

examples.trans: Please help me (do helping for me).
Please do this for me.

meanings.note: Used by a younger male to address an older brother or close older male friend/colleague.

examples.trans: Hey, do you have time tonight?
My older brother is an office worker.
